title: Energy stores and Sankey diagram sheet
subject: Science
unit: Spring 1: Making materials (9E); conservation of energy
source: Seeded from science/y9 lesson 20 (Energy stores and Sankey diagram sheet (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 20: Energy stores and transfers. To understand energy stores, the ways energy is transferred and the principle of conservation of energy

picture.alt: A Sankey diagram of energy transfers
picture.draw: Draw and label: Energy stores and Sankey diagram sheet

questions.q: Describe the energy transfer when a battery-powered torch is switched on.
questions.a: Chemical store in the battery transfers electrically to the bulb, then by light (useful) and heating (wasted) to the surroundings.
questions.model: Start store: chemical (battery). Transfer: electrically. End: light radiated (useful) and thermal store of surroundings (wasted). Total stays the same.

questions.q: A lamp gets 100 J and gives 10 J of light. Where are the other 90 J?
questions.a: Dissipated as thermal energy to the surroundings.

questions.q: Is sound a store or a transfer?
Core: Write the energy stores and transfers for: a kettle boiling, a car braking, a bow firing an arrow, eating breakfast and then walking.
questions.a: Kettle: electrical to thermal store of water; braking: kinetic to thermal store of brakes; bow: elastic to kinetic; food: chemical to kinetic and thermal.
questions.model: Teacher does the kettle first: energy transferred electrically to the thermal store of the water; some dissipated to the kitchen.

questions.q: Extend: Draw a Sankey diagram for a TV: 200 J in, 120 J light and sound, 80 J thermal.
Stretch: Explain, using conservation of energy, why a perpetual motion machine is impossible.
questions.a: Some energy is always dissipated (friction, heating), so without an input it must eventually stop.

questions.q: Big question: where does the energy go when a ball stops bouncing?
questions.a: It is dissipated to the thermal stores of the ball, floor and air, and as sound; the total is conserved.
